failure_summary: The first clean archive stored the same UTF-8 JSON text with LF line endings, while the canary policy bound the Windows working-tree CRLF raw-byte SHA256 for the prior clean-proof artifact. The worker correctly failed before compiling or executing the canary.
root_cause: The new canary binding helper used raw file bytes instead of the repository's established normalized-text digest rule, making the authority binding sensitive to Git line-ending checkout behavior.
repair: Use SHA256 of UTF-8 text after universal-newline normalization for JSON/text bindings, retain raw-byte SHA only for binary private artifacts, add an explicit CRLF/LF parity test, then commit and run a new R2 clean proof.
known_boundary: R1 proves only that the original binding was not checkout-portable. It does not fail the canary's financial logic, call DeepSeek, or authorize any rerun or product promotion.
